# The isolated conversation unit: names, routing, fields and the update inbox, across the nine sources and the wider field (2026)

Research date: 2026-10-21. Read from the nine sources' cached docs (fetched 2026-10-20 into `.generated/sources/`) and their installed types, then from the official docs, specs and source code of twenty-one other frameworks, protocols and products, and the help centers of eight more products for question 5. Every count is by meaning: a hit counts only when the source uses the word for the concept asked about. The raw word counts from `bun packages/scripts/src/terms.ts` are shown as context, since they mostly count other meanings (HTTP routes, OS threads, sessions of every kind).

The concept: a unit of messages kept apart from other such units. It can sit inside one agent's session (the human's messages to AgentZero split into separate lines of work) or run between agents across sessions (a builder and a reviewer talking). Each incoming human message goes to an existing unit when it is a follow-up, or to a new one when it asks something new. The problem it answers: one session's conversation covers several things at once, so an update about one is buried under newer messages about the others.

Labels: [Docs] official documentation · [Types] a published `.d.ts` or package source · [Spec] a protocol specification · [Undocumented] in the types, absent from the docs.

### Tally

| Count                                                                       | thread                                                                      | session                                                           | conversation                          | other                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nine sources, the term each uses for the unit                               | **3** (Claude Code, Mastra, Codex)                                          | **4** (OpenCode, Claude Agent SDK, Cloudflare, OpenAI Agents SDK) | 1 (eve)                               | chat 1 (AI SDK)                                                   |
| Nine sources with two levels, the separate unit's name                      | **3** (Claude Code, Mastra, Codex)                                          | 1 (Cloudflare, inside an agent rather than a session)             | 1 (eve, which spans sessions)         | 0                                                                 |
| Wider field, current entries (18, MCP and the two superseded APIs left out) | **7** (LangGraph, ChatKit, AG-UI, Managed Agents, Chat SDK, Slack, Discord) | **6** (Agent Framework, ADK, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, ACP, AgentCore)  | 3 (OpenAI Conversations, Letta, OTel) | context 1 (A2A), topic 1 (AutoGen)                                |
| Wider field with two levels, the inner unit's name                          | **5** (Managed Agents, Slack, Discord, Chat SDK, CrewAI `agent_threads`)    | 1 (ACP)                                                           | 1 (Letta, "a message thread")         | branch 2 (ADK, AgentCore), task 1 (A2A), topic source 1 (AutoGen) |
| All two-level systems combined                                              | **8 of 16**                                                                 | 2                                                                 | 2                                     | 4                                                                 |

- **The flat count ties, the meaning asked goes to thread.** Counting each source's single unit, session edges thread in the nine (4 to 3) and thread edges session in the wider field (7 to 6), so they tie at 10 of 27. Restricted to systems that keep a separate line of conversation apart from a session or another container, which is the ZeroSDK case, thread wins: 3 of the 5 two-level sources among the nine and 8 of the 16 two-level systems overall. Where a system names both levels, session or conversation is the outer one and thread the inner one (Mastra Session over thread, Codex session tree over threads, Managed Agents session over session threads, Slack conversation over threads, Letta agent over conversations defined as "a message thread").
- **Session is taken.** ZeroSDK's ADR 0004 already gives session to one agent's working context, and every two-level source uses session for the container, so a session-named unit inside a session would be ambiguous.
- **Conversation is the genus.** Nearly every definition, whatever the term, defines its unit as a conversation: Codex ("A conversation between a user and the Codex agent"), Mastra ("A stored conversation"), Claude Code ("A conversation tied to your current directory"), Cloudflare ("a conversation made up of one or more turns"), ADK ("a single conversation thread"), ACP ("a specific conversation or thread"), LangGraph ("a persistent conversation container"), OTel ("a conversation (session, thread)"). Seven definitions in the wider field put the word thread inside them (ADK, ACP, Letta, AG-UI, OTel, AgentCore, Slack's agent sessions).
- **Counter-signal.** Two vendors moved away from thread for the whole-conversation unit in 2026: OpenAI sunset Assistants Threads for Conversations, and Microsoft renamed `AgentThread` to `AgentSession` because "Thread implies that it is used for just chat history." That rationale fits ZeroSDK's split: the session holds all of an agent's state, the thread holds only the messages of one line of work.
- **Several agents.** Units that take several agents: Mastra threads, eve conversations, Managed Agents sessions (one thread per agent), ADK sessions, CrewAI sessions, AutoGen topics, LangGraph threads, AgentCore sessions. Units bound to one agent: Codex threads, OpenCode and Claude sessions, Letta conversations, A2A contexts, ACP sessions, Agent Framework sessions.

### Tally

| Term                                | Nine sources                                                                                                                                                                                  | Wider field                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **route**, a message to a unit      | **3** (Claude Code, Cloudflare, Mastra)                                                                                                                                                       | 2 (Managed Agents, CrewAI for turns)                                                                           |
| route, a conversation to an agent   | 1 (OpenAI Agents SDK)                                                                                                                                                                         | 0                                                                                                              |
| map                                 | 1 (eve)                                                                                                                                                                                       | 0                                                                                                              |
| subscription                        | 0                                                                                                                                                                                             | 1 (AutoGen)                                                                                                    |
| classify, triage, dispatch, assign  | 0 for this meaning (classify appears inside Claude Code's Slack routing; "triage agent" names the router in the OpenAI Agents SDK; Claude Code's Dispatch is "A phone-initiated task router") | 0                                                                                                              |
| none named: the caller picks the id | 4 (Codex, Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode, AI SDK)                                                                                                                                                 | 11 (A2A, LangGraph, Letta, ADK, Slack, Discord, Agent Framework, OpenAI Conversations, LlamaIndex, ACP, AG-UI) |

The two outcomes are named consistently even where the decision is not: **start** (or create, new) for a new unit, **continue** or **resume** for an existing one (Codex, Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode, eve: "Pass the task's `taskId` ... to continue that session. Omitting `taskId` always starts a new child" at https://eve.dev/docs/subagents, A2A "continuation", ADK "Start or Resume", Letta `/new` and `/resume`). The message that belongs to an existing unit is a **follow-up** (Claude Code Projects, LangGraph, Claude Agent SDK: "You can ask a follow-up question").

| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| session id                       | 5 (OpenCode, Claude Agent SDK, Claude Code, Cloudflare, eve)        | 3 (ADK column, AgentCore, LlamaIndex)                                                     | 8     |

The field follows the unit's name: session id and thread id tie at 8 because session and thread tie in the flat unit count. Every system whose unit is a thread and that links its record names the field thread id (`threadId` in the TypeScript sources Mastra, Codex, Chat SDK and AG-UI; `thread_id` in LangGraph, ChatKit and the Assistants API; `thread_ts` in Slack; `session_thread_id` in Managed Agents), except Discord, where a thread is a kind of channel and the message carries `channel_id`. With the unit named thread, the consensus field is **`threadId`** (8 of 9 thread-unit systems that link the record).

No source orders a conversation's messages with a field named `index`. Index names a place inside a smaller parent: eve's `stepIndex` (a step inside a turn) and `startIndex` (a stream cursor), Claude Agent SDK's `result_index` ("where this result falls in the run's delivery order, counting from 0"), the OpenAI Agents SDK's `callIndex`. Integer order inside a session or conversation is `seq` or `sequence` (4 of 9), and the definitions describe it as a **position**: OpenCode "Position in one aggregate's durable log", eve "zero-based position in the session's turn order", Discord "the approximate position of the message in a thread". The wider field orders by timestamp instead.

Turn is never the record: every source that defines it makes it a group of records ("Turns contain items", Codex; "one user message and all the work it triggers", eve; "One request to an agent and its response", Cloudflare). Line names only the storage format ("one per line in the local JSONL"). Item and event are the choices of systems whose rows also hold tool calls and status changes; message is the choice of systems whose rows are what a person or an agent said.

## 4. Draft definition

> A **thread** is one conversation kept apart from the others in a session: the messages about one thing the human asked, in order. One session can hold many threads, and one thread can carry messages from several agents' sessions. Each new message is routed to the thread it follows up, or starts a new thread.

How it is built from the sources' own words:

- "conversation" as the genus: Codex "Thread: A conversation between a user and the Codex agent", Mastra "Thread: A stored conversation containing messages".
- "kept apart" and "in a session": Mastra's Session holds a "current thread binding" and moves "between conversations"; Discord threads "help better organize conversation in a busy channel"; Codex "`thread.sessionId` identifies the current live session tree root".
- "one thing the human asked": Claude Code Projects "starts a thread for each task".
- "several agents' sessions": Managed Agents "each agent works in its own session thread"; Mastra "Multiple agent modes that share one conversation thread"; eve's conversation id spans "all turns and child sessions".
- "routed ... follows up ... starts": Claude Code "Claude routes each message"; "New work goes to a new thread or to a thread already working in that area"; "reusing an existing thread for follow-ups".

The record that matches, in the consensus terms: a **message** with `content`, `id`, `sessionId`, its position in the session, `threadId`, and its position in the thread. For the two positions the sources say `seq` or `sequence` (4 of 9) and none says `index`.

### Tally

The view's name, one vote per product (Codex and Claude Code counted once, with the nine):

| Name                      | Nine sources                                                                                                     | Wider field (10)                                              | Total |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| **inbox**                 | 0 as the main view (Codex: Scheduled "acts as your inbox")                                                       | **7** (Linear, GitHub, Discord, Devin, Cursor, Notion, Asana) | **7** |
| activity                  | 1 (Codex)                                                                                                        | 2 (Slack, Teams)                                              | 3     |
| notifications             | 0                                                                                                                | 1 (Jira)                                                      | 1     |
| a state-grouped list      | 1 (Claude Code: agent view, Overview)                                                                            | 0                                                             | 1     |
| unread(s), mentions, feed | 0 as the view; unread is a tab, filter or section in 8 products, mentions in 4, feed only inside "Activity feed" |                                                               | 0     |
| none                      | 7                                                                                                                | 0                                                             | 7     |

What "inbox" means where it appears in the nine sources:

| Meaning                                            | Sources                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| an agent's or session's queue of incoming messages | **4**: OpenCode (`Session.Inbox`), Claude Code (teammate and cross-session inboxes), eve (command inbox), Mastra (per-thread notification inbox) |
| a human's view of updates                          | 2: Codex (Scheduled "acts as your inbox"), Cloudflare (an example per-user `Inbox` agent over `Chat` sub-agents)                                 |
| none                                               | 3: Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, AI SDK                                                                                                   |

The per-item state:

| State                                          | Count                                       | Where                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **unread / read**                              | **13 of 13** products with a view or marker | every one: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Slack, Linear, GitHub, Discord, Teams, Devin, Cursor, Notion, Asana, Jira |
| archived                                       | 7                                           | Codex, Claude Code, Mastra, Notion, Asana, Linear (automatic), Slack's old Later                                   |
| saved / bookmarked                             | 4                                           | GitHub, Slack, Discord, Asana                                                                                      |
| cleared / dismissed                            | 4                                           | Slack, Discord, Jira, Mastra                                                                                       |
| needs input / waiting on you / needs attention | 6                                           | Codex, Claude Code, Devin, Cursor, Slack code channels, Linear                                                     |
| seen                                           | 1                                           | Mastra (`markSeen`)                                                                                                |
| done                                           | 1                                           | GitHub                                                                                                             |
| snoozed                                        | 1                                           | Linear                                                                                                             |

- **Inbox wins in products, not in the nine.** Seven of the ten wider products name the view Inbox, including the agent products (Devin, Cursor, Linear for agent updates). Among the nine, only Codex has a cross-conversation view, and it calls it Activity; Claude Code shows a list grouped by state instead.
- **Inbox collides inside the nine.** Four of the nine use inbox for an agent's own incoming queue. Mastra even keeps one per thread, which is where a peer agent's message waits when no one picked it up ("the signal stays pending in the target's notification inbox"). A human-facing Inbox in ZeroSDK follows the products; the agent-side queue then needs another word.
- **Unread is universal.** Every product with a view keeps unread and read on each item, and Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode mark a whole chat, session or tab unread. Agent products add a second, separate run state (needs input, working, completed) beside it.
- **GitHub calls each notification a thread**, with `unread` and `last_read_at` on it, which is the shape of ZeroSDK's threads and Inbox.

## 6. Summary

| Question               | Winner                                                                                      | Runner-up                                                                                                                                                                  | Split                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. The unit            | **thread**: 3 of 5 two-level sources among the nine, 8 of 16 two-level systems overall      | session (4 of 9 flat, against thread's 3; 10 of 27 flat overall, tied with thread), but it names the container and is ZeroSDK's agent term; conversation is the genus word | The flat count ties; the nested meaning goes to thread. Two vendors dropped thread for the whole-conversation unit in 2026 (OpenAI, Microsoft). |
| 2. Assigning a message | **route**: 3 of 9 (Claude Code, Cloudflare, Mastra), plus Managed Agents and CrewAI         | none named: the caller picks an id (4 of 9, 11 wider)                                                                                                                      | Outcomes are named start (new) and continue or resume (existing); the message is a follow-up.                                                   |
| 3a. Link field         | **`threadId`**: 8 of 9 thread-unit systems that link the record (Discord uses `channel_id`) | session id (8 overall, tied with thread id)                                                                                                                                | The field follows the unit's name.                                                                                                              |
| 3b. Order field        | **`seq` / `sequence`**: 4 of 9 (OpenCode, Cloudflare, Claude Agent SDK, eve)                | timestamp (8 in the wider field); implicit list order (3 of 9)                                                                                                             | No source uses `index` for a message's place in a conversation; docs call the value a position.                                                 |
| 3c. Record             | **message**: 4 of 9, 15 of 26 overall                                                       | item and event (4 each)                                                                                                                                                    | Item and event come from systems that store tool calls and status changes as rows.                                                              |
| 5. Update view         | **Inbox**: 7 of 10 wider products                                                           | Activity (Codex, Slack, Teams)                                                                                                                                             | In the nine, inbox is an agent's incoming queue (4 of 9); per-item state is unread/read in 13 of 13.                                            |
